## Plan

### Objective

Close the `javascript:`-URL sink on the hosted auth pages' `?redirect=` / `?next=` / `?returnTo=` parameter by generalizing the guard `#943` already shipped for `?back=` into a single shared helper, applied once at the destination-resolution point inside `_mat.redirect()` so that **both** navigation sinks (direct navigation and post-handoff) are covered by one check. A refused destination navigates nowhere and shows an error. Cross-origin `http`/`https` destinations, protocol-relative values and same-origin relative paths behave exactly as they do today — the host is deliberately not allowlisted here.

### What is actually broken (verified in the current tree)

`/Users/ians/Projects/mojo/django-mojo/mojo/apps/account/templates/account/auth_base.html`

- `:92-94` — `paramRedirect` is read from the query string and becomes `redirectTo` with no validation.
- `:164-195` — `_mat.redirect()` resolves `redirectTo` through `new URL(target, window.location.href)` **only to compute `isCrossOrigin`**; it never inspects `resolved.protocol`.
- `:176` — `window.location.href = target` (direct navigation).
- `:183` — `window.location.href = target + sep + 'auth_code=' + …` (post-handoff).
- `:210-221` — `safeBackHref`, which does exactly the missing check, applied only to `?back=`.

A `javascript:` value resolves to `origin === "null"`, so `isCrossOrigin` is true and the handoff branch runs; `redirect_allowlist._split` (`mojo/apps/account/services/redirect_allowlist.py:190-213`) does refuse a hostname-less URL, but `on_auth_handoff` (`mojo/apps/account/rest/user.py:257-262`) mints anyway in the shipped monitor-mode default, so `:183` fires. `:176` fires whenever `MojoAuth.isAuthenticated()` is false (it is just "is there an access token in `localStorage`" — `mojo/apps/account/static/account/mojo-auth.js:780-782`), with no server round-trip at all. Both confirmed.

Also note `:173`: the current `catch` on the resolve falls through with `target` still set to the **raw** value and `isCrossOrigin` false, i.e. a URL `new URL()` rejects reaches `:176` unparsed. The fix removes that path as a side effect.

### Design decisions

**D1 — Guard at the destination-resolution point inside `_mat.redirect()`, not at the param read.**
`redirect()` already owns the one place where the destination is turned into an absolute URL, and both sinks consume the `target` it produces. One check there covers both, satisfies "navigates nowhere and shows an error" precisely, and leaves the `if (!isCrossOrigin || …)` block — the thing `#1062` edits — structurally untouched.

Guarding at the param read (`:93-94`) was rejected: `redirectTo = paramRedirect || ON_SUCCESS` means a refused param would silently fall back to `ON_SUCCESS` and the page would **navigate somewhere**, which contradicts the acceptance criterion. It would also conflate "no param" with "refused param", and would resolve relative paths to absolute at page-load time, changing `_matConfig.redirectTo` for every deployment.

**D2 — Generalize `safeBackHref` in place, renamed `safeNavUrl`; do not copy it.**
The helper's body is already correct and already carries the right rationale comment. Rename it, generalize the comment to cover both parameters and both sink kinds (`href` and `window.location.href`), and keep its exact contract: *raw string → resolved absolute `http(s)` href, or `null`*. Keeping the contract means the two `?back=` call sites change by name only, so `?back=` behavior is byte-identical. Keep it a **function declaration** — `_matConfig` calls it at `:119`, above the definition, and relies on hoisting (the existing comment at `:116` says so).

Name `safeNavUrl` is free repo-wide. Rejected alternatives: keeping `safeBackHref` (misleading once it guards the post-login destination), and returning the `URL` object instead of a string (would force `(safeNavUrl(x) || {}).href` at the `?back=` sites — uglier, and changes a working call site for no gain).

**D3 — `isCrossOrigin` is computed from the guard's output, and the old `try/catch` goes away.**
`safeNavUrl` returns an absolute `http(s)` href produced by `new URL()`, so re-parsing it cannot throw. The malformed-URL case is now handled by the guard returning `null` (fail-closed) instead of by falling through to a raw navigation (fail-open). This is the "minimal restructuring" the batch asks for: three lines replaced by four, the branch below untouched.

**D4 — Error UX: reuse the existing refusal shape and copy, inline.**
`window._mat.hideOverlay()` then `window._mat.showMessage("That destination isn't allowed. Please return to the app and try again.", "error")` — the same two lines and the same string the handoff `.catch` already uses at `:190-193`. It is the same user-visible situation ("we were told to send you somewhere we won't send you"), and reusing the string avoids handing an attacker an oracle that distinguishes a client-side scheme refusal from a server-side allowlist refusal. Deliberately **not** factored into a shared `_mat` method: `#1062`'s C6 wants the `.catch` copy to start surfacing the server's message, while the client-side refusal must keep the static string — a shared helper would have to be un-shared one item later. `hideOverlay()` is safe when no overlay is showing (the passkey-enroll "skip" path calls `redirect()` with no overlay), and every page extending `auth_base.html` renders `#mat-message` (`:57`), so the error is visible on all of them.

**D5 — `_matConfig.redirectTo` is validated but not rewritten (one line, hardening).**
`#943` sanitized `_matConfig.backUrl` for the same reason it fixed the hero link: page scripts read the published value straight into an `href`. `redirectTo` is published on the same object at `:105`. Nothing in this repo reads it and it is not documented as a public field (only `_matConfig.groupUuid` is), so this is precautionary — but publishing an attacker-supplied `javascript:` URL on a config object consumed by page scripts is the same hole one indirection out. Publish `safeNavUrl(redirectTo) ? redirectTo : ""` — **validated, not rewritten**, so a relative path stays relative and the acceptance criterion "same-origin relative paths behave exactly as today" holds for page scripts too. This is the only optional line in the plan; see Open questions.

**D6 — No host allowlisting, no server-side change, no `mojo-auth.js` change.**
Cross-origin destinations are legitimate; the scheme check is the fix, exactly as `#943` recorded for `?back=`. `MojoAuth.requestHandoffCode(destination)` already requires a destination and now always receives a guarded absolute `http(s)` URL, so the JS library is unaffected. Destination allowlisting stays where it is: opt-in, server-side, `AUTH_HANDOFF_ALLOWED_URLS` / `AUTH_HANDOFF_RESOLVER`.

### Edge cases

| Input | Resolved | Behavior after the fix |
|---|---|---|
| param absent | `redirectTo = ON_SUCCESS` (server default `/`) | unchanged — same-origin, direct nav |
| `?redirect=` (empty) | falsy → `ON_SUCCESS` | unchanged. `redirectTo` can only be empty if `ON_SUCCESS` is empty, which the view (`bouncer/views.py:342`, `theme.success_redirect or '/'`) and the template default (`|default:'/'`) both make unreachable |
| `?redirect=%20%20` (whitespace only) | URL parser strips it → base URL | unchanged — navigates to the auth page itself |
| `javascript:alert(1)` | protocol `javascript:` | **refused**, error shown, no navigation |
| `javascript:alert(1)//` (the payload that survives the `?auth_code=` append at `:183`) | `javascript:` | **refused** |
| `JaVaScRiPt:alert(1)` | parser lowercases the scheme | **refused** |
| `java\tscript:alert(1)`, `java\nscript:…` | parser strips tabs/newlines anywhere in the input | **refused** — this is why the guard judges the *resolved* protocol rather than string-matching a prefix |
| `data:text/html,…`, `vbscript:…`, `blob:…`, `filesystem:…` | non-http(s) | **refused** |
| `mailto:…`, `tel:…`, `myapp://…` | non-http(s) | **refused** — see Contract changes |
| `//evil.tld` (protocol-relative) | `https://evil.tld/` | **unchanged** — allowed, cross-origin, handoff branch. The host is not allowlisted here by design |
| `\\evil.tld` / `\/\/evil.tld` (backslash trick) | parser folds backslashes to slashes for special schemes → `https://evil.tld/` | **unchanged** — same as protocol-relative |
| `/dashboard` (relative) | `https://<auth-origin>/dashboard` | **unchanged** — same-origin, direct nav, no handoff |
| `#section` (fragment only) | current URL + fragment | **unchanged** — same-origin, direct nav |
| `https://<auth-origin>/x` (absolute same-origin) | itself | **unchanged** — `isCrossOrigin` false, direct nav |
| `http://[` and other strings `new URL()` rejects | throws | **refused** with an error — previously fell through the `catch` at `:173` and navigated to the raw string |
| destination refused **and** the visitor just signed in | — | tokens are stored, the visitor stays on the auth page with the error. Correct: they authenticated against the real origin, only the destination is bad |

`mojo/apps/account/rest/bouncer/views.py:412-417` re-forwards `redirect`/`next`/`returnTo`/`back` through the bouncer challenge as urlencoded query values on a **same-origin path** (`/{login_path}?…`). That is a pass-through, not a sink; the guard runs when the visitor lands back on the auth page. No change needed there.

### Testing plan

Conventions: `from testit import helpers as th` (already at the top of the file), `@th.django_unit_test("…")` + `def test_xxx(opts):`, imports inside the body, a descriptive failure message on every assert. No fixtures and no `th.server_settings` — this is a pure template-source assertion, so the "setup deletes before creating" rule has nothing to apply to. The file already defines a local `assert_false` helper; these assertions do not need it.

New test in `/Users/ians/Projects/mojo/django-mojo/tests/test_auth/handoff.py`, appended after `test_back_param_is_scheme_guarded`, preceded by a banner comment explaining (as the `?back=` one does) that the sink is client-side JS with no JS runtime in the suite, so the template source is what is checkable and what actually regressed.

Body: `from pathlib import Path` + `import mojo`; resolve the template the same way the `?back=` test does; read the source; then

1. `assert_true("function safeNavUrl(" in src, …)` — the generalized guard exists. *Fails pre-fix.*
2. `assert_true("safeBackHref" not in src, …)` — generalized in place, not left behind as a second helper. *Fails pre-fix.*
3. `assert_eq(src.count('resolved.protocol !== "http:"'), 1, …)` — exactly **one** implementation; a second copy will drift.
4. `assert_true('resolved.protocol !== "http:"' in src and 'resolved.protocol !== "https:"' in src, …)` — it decides on the resolved protocol.
5. `assert_true("var target = redirectTo;" not in src, …)` — the raw destination no longer reaches the sinks. *Fails pre-fix.*
6. Isolate the function body: `body = src.split("redirect: function ()", 1)[1].split("onAuthSuccess:", 1)[0]`, then
   - `guard_at = body.find("safeNavUrl(redirectTo)")`, `first_sink = body.find("window.location.href = ")`
   - `assert_true(0 <= guard_at < first_sink, …)` — the guard runs **before** the first navigation sink. *Fails pre-fix* (`guard_at == -1`).
   - `assert_true("showMessage" in body[guard_at:first_sink] and '"error"' in body[guard_at:first_sink], …)` — a refused destination shows an error rather than silently doing nothing.
   - `assert_eq(body.count("window.location.href = target"), body.count("window.location.href = "), …)` — **every** sink in `redirect()` navigates to the guarded `target`. This one passes pre-fix by construction; it is the durable invariant that will catch a future edit (including `#1062`'s) adding an unguarded sink.
7. `assert_true('params.get("redirect")' in src and 'params.get("next")' in src and 'params.get("returnTo")' in src, …)` — all three aliases still feed the guarded path; the fix must not have quietly dropped one.

The window in (6) is chosen so `#1062`'s edits survive it: that item adds a clause to the `if (!isCrossOrigin || …)` condition (which sits between the refusal block and the first sink) and rewrites the `.catch` message (outside the window entirely).

Updated test: `test_back_param_is_scheme_guarded` — symbol rename only, same four assertions, same intent. Its `src.count("safeNavUrl(paramBack)") == 2` continues to pin that `?back=` runs through the shared helper at both of its sinks, which is the AC's "one implementation" requirement from the other side.

Run (BUILD agent, not the scoper): `bin/run_tests --agent -t test_auth.handoff`, reading `var/test_failures.json` for diagnostics. Expected sequence: new test fails after Step 1; whole file passes after Steps 2, 3 and 5. `tests/test_auth/csp.py`, `tests/test_auth/passkey_error_ux.py`, `tests/test_auth/oauth_callback_single_fire.py` and `tests/test_auth_config/auth_config.py` also assert against `auth_base.html`, but on the CSP nonce, `sanitizeMessage`, the OAuth completion path and the `mat-login-methods` block — none touch the redirect path or the guard. A `-t test_auth` run covers them all if the agent wants the wider net.

Both tracks change, because user-visible behavior changes.

**web_developer** — `/Users/ians/Projects/mojo/django-mojo/docs/web_developer/account/auth_pages.md`
- URL-parameter table, the `?redirect=<url>` row (`:65`): add that only `http`/`https` URLs and same-origin relative paths are accepted.

Note that this is a **scheme** check only — the destination host is not restricted by it, and host restriction remains the separate opt-in server-side allowlist described in the Cross-Origin Redirect Handoff section just above.

**django_developer** — `/Users/ians/Projects/mojo/django-mojo/docs/django_developer/account/auth.md`
- In the handoff/enforcement section (around `:270-300`, near the existing "This is also how `javascript:` and `data:` are refused — they have no hostname" line): add a short paragraph stating that the auth page refuses a non-`http`/`https` destination **client-side, before any request is made**, in every allowlist mode. This matters for operators reading that page because monitor mode mints for anything — so the sentence to write is that monitor mode is no longer the only thing standing between a `javascript:` destination and the browser sink, and the client guard covers the unauthenticated direct-navigation path that never reaches the server at all.

**CHANGELOG** — `/Users/ians/Projects/mojo/django-mojo/CHANGELOG.md`, under `## Unreleased`, in the voice of the `#943` entry at `:509-518`:

`**fix (account/security)** — **`?redirect=` on the hosted auth pages can no longer carry a `javascript:` URL.**` … the page read `?redirect=`/`?next=`/`?returnTo=` straight from the query string and assigned it to `window.location.href` at both the direct-navigation and post-handoff sinks with no protocol check, so a crafted link ran attacker script on the auth origin — the origin whose `localStorage` holds the visitor's tokens. `?back=`'s scheme guard is now shared by both parameters (one implementation, renamed `safeNavUrl`); a destination that does not resolve to `http`/`https` is refused, the page navigates nowhere and shows an error. The host is deliberately **not** allowlisted — a cross-origin destination is legitimate and the scheme check is what closes the hole; host restriction remains the separate opt-in `AUTH_HANDOFF_ALLOWED_URLS`. Mention that a non-web scheme such as `mailto:` or a custom app scheme is refused too.

No doc-folder `README.md` index change — no new doc files.

### Commit plan

One commit. `git add` and `git commit -- <exact paths>`, never a directory pathspec, never `-A`.

```
fix(security): scheme-guard the ?redirect= destination on the hosted auth pages
```

Body: what the sink was (both `window.location.href` assignments in `_mat.redirect()`), why it fired in the shipped default (monitor-mode handoff mints anyway; the direct-navigation branch never reaches the server), that the `?back=` guard was generalized in place to `safeNavUrl` rather than copied, and that the host is deliberately not allowlisted. End with the `Co-Authored-By:` trailer naming the builder's model.

Paths: the template, `tests/test_auth/handoff.py`, the two docs, `CHANGELOG.md`.

### Composition with #1062 (builds after this, same batch)

`#1062` touches `auth_base.html` in two places: the session-check block at `:234-248` (skip the refresh under a group-token session) and `_mat.redirect()`'s direct-navigation condition (`if (!isCrossOrigin || !MojoAuth.isAuthenticated())`), plus its C6 change to the `.catch` message. This plan leaves all three of those lines byte-identical — it only replaces the four lines *above* the condition and renames a helper 40 lines below. The one interaction worth stating for that item's builder: the client-side refusal at the top of `redirect()` must keep the static string even after C6 makes the `.catch` surface the server's message, so that a client-side scheme refusal and a server-side authorization refusal are not distinguishable to a caller.

## Schema/migration impact

**None.** Verified: the change touches one Django template, one test module, two docs and the CHANGELOG. No model, field, index, or `Meta` change; no new or changed setting (so no `bin/create_testproject` regeneration and no `th.server_settings` in the test); no migration to generate or apply.

## Contract changes

1. **A `?redirect=`/`?next=`/`?returnTo=` value that does not resolve to `http:` or `https:` is now refused.** The page navigates nowhere and shows "That destination isn't allowed. Please return to the app and try again." Previously it navigated. For `javascript:` and `data:` that is precisely the fix — a "working" `javascript:` redirect was arbitrary script execution on the auth origin, and refusing it is the point.
2. **Non-web schemes are refused too** — `mailto:`, `tel:`, and custom app schemes such as `myapp://`. A deployment that used `?redirect=` to bounce a visitor into a native app via a custom scheme breaks. This is intended (fail-closed; an allowlist of "safe" non-web schemes is exactly the drift the single-implementation criterion exists to prevent); such a deployment should point `?redirect=` at an `https` universal/app link instead. Call it out in the CHANGELOG so an operator hitting it can recognize it immediately.
3. **A destination that `new URL()` rejects is now refused instead of navigated to raw.** Previously the `catch` at `:173` left `target` as the unparsed input and fell through to direct navigation. Fail-open → fail-closed.
4. **The template-local helper `safeBackHref` is renamed `safeNavUrl`.** It is a closure inside an IIFE in a template — not exported, not on `window`, not reachable by any page script — so no runtime consumer can break. The only reference outside the template is `tests/test_auth/handoff.py`, updated in the same commit.
5. **`?back=` behavior is unchanged** — same guard, same contract, same two call sites, name only.
6. **`_matConfig.redirectTo`** (Step 4, if kept): a value that fails the guard is published as `""` instead of the raw string. A value that passes is published **unchanged** — relative stays relative — so no legitimate page script sees a difference. If Step 4 is dropped, this field is unchanged entirely.

## Premise check

- **Verified true:** the unguarded read at `:92-94`; both sinks at `:176` and `:183`; `safeBackHref` at `:210-221`; `redirect_allowlist._split` refusing hostname-less URLs (`services/redirect_allowlist.py:190-213`, with a comment literally naming `javascript:` and `data:`); monitor mode minting anyway (`rest/user.py:257-262`), deliberately pinned by `tests/test_auth/handoff.py:395-422`; the `?back=` test precedent at `:628-658`. Line numbers have not drifted.
- **Stale premise (#945 has shipped, but the conclusion still holds).** The workspec says "there is no CSP anywhere in the framework to blunt it (see #945)". CSP landed in `47382a1c` — `auth_base.html` now emits `nonce="{{ csp_nonce }}"` on both `<script>` tags and `mojo/apps/account/services/csp.py` sends a nonce-locked `script-src` with no `'unsafe-inline'`, which does block `javascript:`-URL navigation. **But `AUTH_CSP_ENABLED` ships `False`** — `8c1c52fb` documents that the entire opt-in lives in a gitignored per-deployment config — so on the shipped default there is still no CSP and the sink is fully live. On an opted-in deployment the CSP is defense in depth only; it does not remove the need for this fix, and the direct-navigation branch at `:176` is reachable with no server involvement either way. Worth correcting the sentence when the item is closed; it changes nothing about the plan.
- **Omission in the workspec: renaming `safeBackHref` breaks an existing test.** `tests/test_auth/handoff.py:651` asserts `"function safeBackHref(" in src` and `:656` asserts `src.count("safeBackHref(paramBack)") == 2`. The AC mandates a rename but does not mention this. Step 5 handles it; the two template edits and the test update must land together or `test_auth.handoff` goes red mid-build.
- **A second instance of the same bug class exists, outside this item's scope — do not fix here.** `/Users/ians/Projects/mojo/django-mojo/mojo/apps/account/rest/verify.py:23` (`_render_verify`) reads `redirect_url = request.GET.get("redirect", "")` with no validation and puts it on the context; `email_verify_confirm.html` and `email_change_confirm.html` render it into `<a href="{{ redirect_url }}">` at `:111` and `:132`, which is the same click-to-execute sink `#943` closed for `?back=`. (The `<meta http-equiv="refresh" …url={{ redirect_url }}>` at `:83` in both is not a live sink — browsers refuse non-`http(s)` in a meta refresh — but the anchors are.) Two further notes for whoever picks it up: this is a **server-side, Python** fix, not a template-JS one, so it cannot share `safeNavUrl`; and it violates the repo convention by reading `request.GET` instead of `request.DATA`. Recommend filing as its own item.
- **No other template in the hosted auth flow shares the hole.** `passkey_enroll.html` calls the same `_mat.redirect()` (`:78`, `:91`, `:103`) and is therefore fixed by this change with no edit of its own. `bouncer_challenge.html`'s `CFG.redirectUrl` (`:184`, sinks at `:346`/`:349`) is a server-built same-origin path (`bouncer/views.py:423`, `/{redirect_path}{group_qs}`). `register.html:416` navigates to `cfg.passkeyUrl`, server-rendered config. `contact.html` never redirects. `bouncer_decoy.html` has no redirect. `mojo-bouncer.js:709`'s `blockRedirectUrl` is deployment config, not a query param.
- **Not a hole, noted so it is not mistaken for one:** `var ON_SUCCESS = "{{ success_redirect|default:'/' }}";` (`:72`) lacks `|escapejs`, unlike its neighbors at `:84` and `:101`. Django's autoescaping turns `<` and `"` into entities, which the HTML parser does not decode inside `<script>`, so there is no string or tag breakout — and after this change the value is scheme-guarded on its way to the sink as well. No action.
- **Pre-existing cosmetic:** three literal `—` sequences sit inside `//` comments at `:165`, `:173` and `:188` (they render as literal text, not em dashes). Two are on lines this change rewrites and disappear naturally; write real em dashes in the replacements.

## Open questions for the gate

1. **Keep the one-line `_matConfig.redirectTo` hardening (Step 4)?** Nothing in this repo reads that field and it is not documented as public, so it is precautionary — but `#943` sanitized the sibling field `_matConfig.backUrl` for exactly this reason, and the published value would otherwise still be an attacker-supplied `javascript:` URL one indirection away from any consumer page script. Written as `safeNavUrl(redirectTo) ? redirectTo : ""` it validates without rewriting, so relative paths stay relative and no legitimate consumer sees a change. **Recommendation: keep it.** Dropping it costs nothing to the acceptance criteria (both named sinks are covered by Step 3 alone) and yields the absolute minimum diff, so it is a clean thing to cut if you want this commit to touch nothing beyond `_mat.redirect()` and the helper.
